findings.screen: optuna-screener → experiment → systems → kill-list (y14.5k–19.6k at 1440, y14.6k–18.6k at 1024)
findings.finding: The longest star-less stretch: 30 and 25 consecutive 1 s clips in which nothing performs. Prose, a blueprint panel, a green chart, a photo and a panel stack scroll past at page speed. The log credits B23–B29 here (annotation oval, chart, drone photo, systems panel) but none of them shows as an animation by eye (clips.json motion is 0.012 or less on 25 of the 30 clips at 1440 and 22 of 25 at 1024; 10 and 8 of them carry a log star tagged '(static)'). No declared breath covers it. About 12% of all reader clips sit in this one stretch.

findings.screen: work: 'Led by what survived scrutiny' dwell and the validation gauntlet (y9.7k–10.3k at 1440, y8.8k–10.3k at 1024)
findings.finding: The 2 s stop on the pen heading is credited to B16-pen (a live-only loop) and shows a still screen for 5 clips at 1440 and 4 at 1024 (the sheet says '(static)'). At 1024 the star-less run continues through the chalkboard scroll and the colonnade for 14 s. The pen glint the loop is meant to supply is not visible in any frame.

findings.screen: principles (the Marauder's map) through contact and credits
findings.finding: After the parchment unrolls (a good single star, #224–#227), 13 to 16 s of parchment pages follow with nothing I can see move: B54-hall is a still for the 4 s stop (#228–#231), and the footprints and ink marks the log credits to B54/B55 change fewer than about 1% of pixels, too faint to read as a star at 200 px. Contact and credits then scroll static. The declared breath after B50 (#223–#226) ends as the parchment finishes unrolling, before this stretch.

findings.screen: the 2 s dwell stops (every h2 and act-card settle)
findings.clip: reader 1440: 68 clips and reader 1024: 55 clips carry a log star tagged '(static)', e.g. 1440 #37–#40 (B08-invite compass), #64 (B14-loop), #129–#131 (B28-pen), #167–#168 and #174–#175 (B38-fireflies), #219–#221 (B50-motes), #228–#231 (B54-hall), #242–#244 (B56-flame)
findings.finding: The stops are where the page should perform a calm single star, and by eye almost every one is a still. The 14 loop stars the manifest marks 'live only, lent a still screen' (B04-loop, B10-sea, B14-loop, B16-pen, B17-beam, B20-window, B22-board, B25-demo, B28-pen, B38-fireflies, B50-motes, B50-loop, B54-hall, B56-flame) never read as motion in these recordings. This includes the compass invite on About (B08-invite) and the pen, which the game discovery relies on. The log's 73% / 72% 'exactly one star' therefore overstates what the eye gets: roughly a third of its 'one star' clips are stills.

Five or six seconds of a motionless hero (name, sea, text) after the 'THE CROSSING' caption fade. The log credits B02 (mostly '(static)'), no breath is declared before B04, and no ambient loop is visible. This reads as the first dead screen after the intro, not a deliberate rest.

findings.screen: About (builder of quantitative systems) into the journey intro
findings.finding: After the heading's gold wipe (#35 / #31) there are 9–10 star-less seconds: prose scrolling and a 4 s stop on the h2 where the compass invite (B08-invite) is credited but the compass does not move at either width.

findings.screen: act 1 ship card, after the iris expands
findings.finding: Once the porthole ring has expanded to the full ship the screen is a still for 3 s (B04 and B04-loop credited, nothing moves) before 'The Crossing' title reveals (#29 / #27). The expansion itself (#22–#25) is a clean single star; the dwell that follows is not.

findings.screen: writing journal: running horse and page sketch
findings.finding: Two stars at once by eye: the small running horse (B45) crosses the bottom of the page while the entry sketch (B44-page4 at 1440, B44-page3 at 1024) draws itself at the top right in the same second. Both are small and in the same ink idiom, but they are two different elements moving together; the log lists both beats without an overlap. In the neighbouring clips (#188, #190, #200, #202) only one of them moves.

The finale star (B58, weight 3) is a faint comet streak that I could only resolve after brightening the frames about three times; at sheet contrast the last 3–4 seconds read as a black screen with one line of type. The breath that follows B58 (y44,057–44,957 at 1440; y41,482–42,250 at 1024) lies below the maximum scroll (43,312 / 40,857), so the final clips are star-less outside any declared breath. Either start the breath earlier or make the comet legible.

findings.screen: act 3 card: ember dot and light-leak band
findings.finding: The ember dot (B35) flies down across the heading while the horizontal light band (B36) fades in over the same image. Two bright moving things in one second; the log has only B35 in this clip. At 1440 the band is already present when the ember flies (#162–#163), so there it reads as one star.

The machine's only red '2+ AT ONCE' bands (log overlaps of 8–150 ms) are not visible as two moving things. At reader #57 / #54 and skimmer #26 the sunset sea image already holds still and I see no star at all; at skimmer #37, #73 and #101 I see one. The 2+ bar is passed on the log (1 clip per reader run) for the wrong reason: the real 2+ clips are the horse/sketch and ember/band ones above, which the log does not flag.

findings.screen: motion the spotlight does not arbitrate
findings.finding: Clips the sheet labels 'NO STAR' in which I do see one thing performing: the ocean caustics shimmer, the colonnade photo fading in, the classroom-to-people image crossfade, the lens widget leaving its list, the hero's sea glow fading up. These are host animations outside the spotlight, so the log cannot count or arbitrate them. They help the one-star count but are untracked (clips.json has moving=true on them; the sheets print plain 'NO STAR', never '(moves)').

The new '(moves)' label word never appears on any of the 72 sheets (I measured the width of every red NO STAR band: all 56 / 54 reader and 15 / 3 skimmer bands carry the same seven-character text). clips.json flags 18 (1440) and 18 (1024) of those reader clips, and 8 / 2 skimmer clips, as moving with no star, so they print as a plain red 'NO STAR' and the machine's own claim cannot be read from the label. The manifest's 21 / 22 and 12 / 5 'motion, no star' totals include breath rows that have no red band.

One star by eye in 46% (1440) and 47% (1024) of fling clips, 55 and 42 clips with nothing outside a breath, and no clip with two competing stars by eye. At fling speed the stars that do read are the large card moves (ring, liquid wipe, iris, sea morph, lens) and typing; prose and diagrams are scroll only. No bar is set for the skimmer; nothing competes.

findings.clip: reader 1440 #20–#25 (hero lift, porthole ring, ring to ship), #51–#56 (sea image morph), #61–#62 (liquid wipe), #71–#72 (heading types in), #133–#138 (lens widget), #217 (iris to the hall); the same beats at 1024
findings.finding: The big beats are exactly one clear star each: the porthole-to-ship iris, the continuous sea-image morph through the journey, the liquid-edge wipe into the lecture hall, the typed 'Led by what survived scrutiny.', the lens tracking the kill-list, and the campfire-to-hall iris. Nothing else competes on those screens.

read: screencast/{reader,skimmer}-{1440,1024}/clips.json (labels, breath rows, motion flag, section, y)
notes.introSkipped: clips 1-12 of both reader runs (play screen, flight, reveal, titles); skimmer runs have no intro

definitions.zero: no element I can see performing beyond rigid scroll; zero includes clips inside declared breaths, zeroInBreath says how many
definitions.oneStar: exactly one element visibly performing (reveal, wipe, iris, typing, morph, draw-in, widget, flicker I could resolve); pure scroll, sticky and parallax layers count as none
definitions.twoPlus: two separate elements (different beat ids) visibly performing in the same second

notes.method: Four frames per clip read at sheet size; ambiguous clips enlarged 1.9x from the sheet. Where my eye could not decide and the clip was marked weak, clips.json motion >= 0.01 kept it as a star and below 0.01 made it a zero. The finale comet was resolved only with a 3x brightness boost on a crop of the frames.
notes.bracket: reader one-star share: eye 33.1% / 34.1% (strict); about 39% if every machine-detected motion of 2% of pixels or more is counted as a star; 51.0% / 55.2% by the machine's own motion flag; 73.5% / 72.0% by the spotlight log. All four are below the 90% bar.
